about: Truman Show Christof is a close-up of Ed Harris as Christof, the creator of the show inside The Truman Show, wearing a beret, round wire glasses and a headset with a red light, one hand raised thoughtfully to his chin as he gazes up at the monitors. His look is calm, attentive and a little proud, the expression of someone who controls every detail of another person's life and is watching it play out. The meme casts Christof as whatever seems to secretly orchestrate your experience: algorithms, game designers, the universe, your parents. It is also used to suggest that a coincidence was far too perfectly timed to be accidental.
origin: The image is from The Truman Show (1998), directed by Peter Weir, with Ed Harris as Christof and Jim Carrey as Truman Burbank.
usage:
Top box names who is watching, typically the all-knowing force in your life. Bottom box describes the tiny thing you just did that they are reacting to, or the command they are about to give, often in the form "now ___". The idea is that your ordinary moment is being directed or monitored from above.

It shines for suspiciously targeted ads, uncanny game spawns, perfectly timed weather, and any moment that feels scripted. Keep the action in the bottom box short and specific.
ideas: when i finally fix my build
watching me leave my umbrella at home
when i open a new tab during the test
right as i say "what could go wrong"
